subject: MAP: Performance proof plan, run results, and close timeline
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@finstack.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finstack.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: performance proof plan and initial asks

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks for the chat this morning. Per our MAP, attached is a concise performance proof plan so we can validate Redwood Dedicated against your real workload and commit to the March-augmented SLA you requested. High-level asks:

- Test corpus: a 48-hour representative sample of FinStack production prompts (we can accept a filtered subset; sample format attached).
- Target scenarios: (A) 1:1 user chat steady-state, (B) batch ingest/policy rerank bursts.
- Desired SLOs to validate: median generation latency < 220 ms (50 tokens), TTFT < 40 ms for cached prefixes, sustained QPS target 120 reqs/s for chat scenario at 8 concurrent model workers.
- Allowed concurrency and window: plan calls for three 20-minute sustained runs and one 2-hour soak.

We've attached: redwood-throughput-plan.csv (run matrix) and costing projection for 1M and 10M token baselines. Please confirm the sample dataset and the time window that works for your engineering team.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the sample by EOD Monday (we'll ingest into a staging cluster).
2) Redwood runs the scheduled benchmark and shares raw traces + condensed results within 48 hours.
3) We mutually review results and finalize pricing/commit by the MAP close date next week.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Steph — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications before we drop the sample: 

1) Our traffic profile is spiky: day peak ~180 qps, sustained off-peak ~30 qps. We can provide the 48-hour dump, but can you confirm whether the soak run needs to reproduce the 180 qps short spikes or just the steady 120 qps you listed?
2) For test model, we'll use FS-chat-2 (32k context) in gen-only mode; is your staging runtime configured with the quantized variant you indicated on the call?

We'll attach the traffic profile and a trimmed sample (see finstack-traffic-profile.json). We can share the full dump Monday morning.

Oliver

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance proof plan and initial asks

Oliver — great context, thanks. Short answers:
- Soak: reproduce spiky peaks for one of the 20-min sustained runs (we'll inject the 180 qps peak for a 3-minute burst inside a 20-min window), and run two steady-state 120 qps runs for comparison.
- Staging runtime: yes — we loaded the quantized variant and tune flags for KV-cache hot paths; results in staging have been promising.

Example targets we'll report back on after runs:
- Throughput: tokens/sec (aggregate) and sustained QPS across window
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 generation latency for 50-token mean responses
- TTFT: first-token arrival median and tail
- Concurrency: end-to-end latency when increasing concurrent workers from 1 -> 12
- Unit economics: cost per 1M tokens (in USD) on the proposed Dedicated profile

We plan to run the initial schedule Monday 16:00–18:30 PT once you drop the sample. Marcus will publish the condensed result + CSV traces.

Thanks —
Stephanie
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@finstack.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finstack.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Staging run snapshot and preliminary numbers

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 13:20, Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> We plan to run the initial schedule Monday 16:00–18:30 PT once you drop the sample.

Quick staging note from our internal pre-check (no production sample yet) — ran a synthetic profile approximating your day peak: 180 qps spike, steady 120 qps baseline. Config: 4 GPU workers (A100-equivalent), quantized FP16-like path.

Results (staging synthetic):
- Sustained QPS (20-min steady run): 122 reqs/s (±3), tokens/sec aggregate: 1,040,000 t/s (note: tokenization variance included)
- Spike run (3-minute 180 qps): p50 latency = 210 ms, p95 = 385 ms, p99 = 620 ms
- TTFT: median 32 ms, p95 58 ms for cached prefixes
- Peak concurrency test (12 workers simulated): tail p99 increases to ~1.1s but median remains <250 ms
- Unit economics (staging estimate, normalized): $7.30 per 1M tokens on the Dedicated profile we modeled; with modest batching and prefix cache active this falls to ~$5.40/1M tokens at sustained loads

I'll attach the raw CSV trace for the staging run (staging-run-20260710.csv) and a short PDF summary we'll present during the mutual review. These are pre-sample numbers; expect +/-10–15% variance once we run against real prompts.

Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

This is helpful — thanks Marcus. A few items from our side before we sign off on the MAP: 

1) Trial pricing: can Redwood offer a 30% trial discount on the first 3 months for the Dedicated commitment? That would let us validate economics in production.
2) Security: please share the most recent SOC2 section on data retention and audit logs — Priya will review. Your link above is helpful but we need the specific retention window details.
3) Contract mechanics: we'll need a redline to the SOW and a standard PO flow for procurement. Can you send the DocuSign / SOW link so our legal team can start?

If we can get those answered by EOD Tuesday, we'll aim to finalize pricing and sign the MAP by Wednesday.

Oliver
